// why: The reference input of the negative control: a minimal but CORRECT picture of a project without zone.js. Every case beside it is built on a copy of this one and brings in exactly one defect, so a case file holds the defect alone rather than one more copy of a correct input. Were this reference itself defective, every case would fire because of it — which is why the gate checks it separately.
// entrypoints: The same path as in `bundle`, but from the second source — the `exports` map. That agreement is the content of point 3: as long as the two lists overlap, the scan walks what the package really publishes. The comment is also here so that a typo in one of them does not look like a case.
// sources: Source text, each file as its lines, read by the gate's own reader (`readSources`), the one the repository's files go through: a case states a decorator the way the sources carry it, and the control exercises the read. A case's `files` replace the file of the same path or join them.
